evals.name: full-scan-ts
evals.prompt: What design patterns does this codebase use? For each one, tell me whether it's actually appropriate here.
evals.expected_output: A report covering every planted pattern in shop-ts with a location, a confidence level, and a verdict that matches the ground truth.
expectations: Identifies Strategy in src/pricing (PricingStrategy with Regular/Member/Bulk) and judges it appropriate
Identifies the Singleton in src/config/AppConfig.ts and flags it as over-engineered or misused, citing its mutable global state or the getInstance() calls inside OrderService
Identifies the payment gateways (StripeGateway/PayPalGateway) as Adapter over the vendor SDKs and judges them appropriate
Identifies Decorator in src/http (Retrying/Logging HttpClient wrapping FetchHttpClient) and judges it appropriate
Says the order status classes in src/orders are really State (not Strategy), or that State would fit better, because OrderService drives the transitions
Says ShippingProxy is functionally a Decorator (logging/timing), not a Proxy
Flags UserFactory as name-only or a trivial/simple factory that is not a GoF Factory Method or Abstract Factory
Identifies the Visitor in src/reports and flags it as over-engineered because there is only one visitor (TotalVisitor)
Identifies the Node EventEmitter usage in src/events as Observer (idiomatic) and does not mark it down for lacking class ceremony
Points out the repeated switch on channel in src/notifications/notify.ts as an opportunity for polymorphism/Strategy
References findings with file paths (ideally file:line)

evals.name: targeted-misapplied-state
evals.prompt: We modeled order statuses in src/orders using the strategy pattern. Is that the right pattern for this?
evals.expected_output: A direct answer that the code is really a state machine, so State fits better than Strategy, backed by evidence from the transition logic in OrderService.
expectations: Answers the question directly: Strategy is not the best fit, or it is misapplied
Recommends the State pattern (or an explicit state machine)
Cites that transitions are driven from OrderService (setStatusStrategy calls) rather than by the status objects themselves
Mentions the string comparison on status.name (e.g. status.name === 'pending' / 'paid') as a sign the abstraction leaks
Gives a concrete recommendation, e.g. moving transition methods (pay/ship/cancel) into the status objects

evals.name: name-trap
evals.prompt: Do src/shipping/ShippingProxy.ts and src/users/UserFactory.ts correctly implement the Proxy and Factory patterns?
evals.expected_output: Both classes are named after patterns they don't implement: ShippingProxy adds logging/timing (Decorator), and UserFactory only wraps a constructor.
expectations: Says ShippingProxy does not control access (no lazy loading, remote, protection, or caching) and so is not really a Proxy
Identifies ShippingProxy as a Decorator (it adds logging/timing behind the same interface)
Says UserFactory is not a GoF Factory Method or Abstract Factory: no polymorphism or subclass choice, just a wrapper around new User()
Recommends renaming ShippingProxy or replacing UserFactory with direct construction, or explains when keeping the factory would be justified

evals.name: python-idiomatic-and-overengineering
evals.prompt: Which GoF patterns does this ETL package use? I'm worried we over-engineered it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the idiomatic Python patterns as legitimate and appropriate, confirms the Template Method, and flags only QueryBuilder as over-engineered.
expectations: Identifies BaseExporter with CsvExporter/JsonLinesExporter as Template Method and judges it appropriate
Identifies QueryBuilder as an over-engineered Builder (only two fields; Python keyword arguments or a dataclass would do)
Recognizes the @retry function decorator as an idiomatic Decorator
Recognizes read_records() as an idiomatic Iterator (generator over the paginated API)
Recognizes the key= function passed to dedupe() as an idiomatic Strategy
Treats the module-level frozen `settings` instance as acceptable (idiomatic Singleton or simply a module constant), not as a harmful mutable global
Does not call the whole package over-engineered; the verdicts discriminate between the pieces

evals.name: full-scan-java-subtle
evals.prompt: Audit the design patterns in this editor codebase: which ones are used, and are they used well?
evals.expected_output: Finds the subtler planted patterns (Bridge, Factory Method inside a Template Method, Mediator named as a Facade), separates appropriate uses from degraded or over-engineered ones, and reports the inverted undo bug.
expectations: Identifies Composite: Group holds child Shapes and implements draw/move/bounds by delegating to them; judged appropriate

Identifies the Shape × Canvas relationship as Bridge (shapes and canvases vary independently) or as Builder (Canvas build steps plus a toBytes() result, with two concrete builders producing different representations), with reasoning, not merely as Strategy or dependency injection
Identifies Command with History as invoker (undo/redo stacks) for Move/Delete/Stroke commands and judges it appropriate
Flags AutosaveCommand as over-engineered or name-only: it does not implement Command, has no undo, and is executed immediately and never stored
Flags the SnapPolicy Strategy as degraded because Editor.drag special-cases `instanceof GridSnap`
Flags the Exporter Template Method as degraded because PngExporter overrides export() itself, bypassing the skeleton (and its own createCanvas)
Identifies Exporter.createCanvas() as a Factory Method used by the template
Says StylePanelFacade is actually a Mediator (widgets call widgetChanged and it coordinates the other widgets), not a Facade
Reports the MoveCommand.undo bug: it moves by (+dx, +dy) instead of (-dx, -dy)
Does not claim GoF patterns in the util package (Colors/Geometry/Ids are static utility classes)

evals.name: targeted-degraded-strategy
evals.prompt: Is our snapping code (src/main/java/com/example/editor/snap) a good use of the Strategy pattern?
evals.expected_output: Strategy is the right pattern and is genuinely used (three policies), but Editor.drag erodes it with an instanceof GridSnap special case. Move that logic into GridSnap.
expectations: Confirms Strategy is the right pattern here (three interchangeable policies selected through setSnap)
Finds the `instanceof GridSnap` special case in Editor.drag even though it is outside the snap package
Calls this erosion/degradation of the pattern (the context depends on a concrete strategy)
Recommends moving the half-cell offset logic into GridSnap.snap so Editor treats every SnapPolicy uniformly

evals.name: no-false-positives
evals.prompt: Which design patterns are used in the util package?
evals.expected_output: The util package has no GoF patterns; the answer says so plainly and does not invent any.
expectations: States that the util package uses no GoF design patterns (or only non-GoF idioms such as static utility classes)
Does not label Ids as a Singleton, or explicitly explains that a static utility class with a static counter is not one
Does not label Ids.next() or Colors.darken() as a Factory
